title: Sum of Two Numbers
description: Write a function `solve(a, b)` that takes two numbers and returns their sum.
hints: Use the addition operator (+).
Remember to return the value directly.

title: Reverse a String
description: Write a function `solve(str)` that accepts a string and returns the reversed string.
hints: Strings can be converted into arrays using split('').
Arrays have a .reverse() method, and can be joined back using .join('').

title: Find Maximum in Array
description: Write a function `solve(arr)` that returns the largest number in a given array of numbers.
hints: You can use Math.max with the spread operator (...arr).
Alternatively, loop through the array tracking the highest value found so far.

title: Palindrome Checker
description: Write a function `solve(str)` that returns `true` if the string is a palindrome (reads the same backwards and forwards), and `false` otherwise. Ignore case sensitivity.
hints: Convert the string to lowercase first using .toLowerCase().
Compare the normalized string to its reversed version.

title: Count Vowels
description: Write a function `solve(str)` that counts and returns the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a given string (case-insensitive).
hints: You can define a string 'aeiou' or a set of vowels.
Loop through each character and check if it is included in vowels.

title: Two Sum
description: Write a function `solve(nums, target)` that returns the indices of the two numbers in `nums` that add up to `target`. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return indices in ascending order `[i, j]`.
hints: A hash map / JavaScript object or Map can store numbers you've seen and their index: map[target - num].
This allows solving it in O(n) linear time.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Write a function `solve(s)` that determines if the input string containing brackets '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']' is valid. An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of brackets in the correct order.
hints: Use a Stack (array with push and pop).
When encountering a closing bracket, check if it matches the top of the stack.

title: Array Chunking
description: Write a function `solve(arr, size)` that splits an array into sub-arrays of maximum length `size`.
hints: You can increment your loop counter by `size` on each iteration.
Use `arr.slice(i, i + size)` to extract each chunk.

title: FizzBuzz Array
description:
Write a function `solve(n)` that returns an array of string representations of numbers from 1 to `n`.
- For multiples of 3, use "Fizz"
- For multiples of 5, use "Buzz"
- For multiples of both 3 and 5, use "FizzBuzz"
- Otherwise, use the number as a string.
hints: Check `i % 15 === 0` (or both % 3 and % 5) first before checking individual 3 and 5.
Build an array using a loop from 1 to n.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Write a function `solve(s)` that finds the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters.
hints: Use a sliding window approach with two pointers `left` and `right`.
Store the last seen index of each character in a Map or object.

title: Flatten Nested Array
description: Write a function `solve(arr)` that flattens an arbitrarily deeply nested array of numbers into a single flat array without using `Array.prototype.flat`.
hints: You can solve this recursively or using an iterative stack.
Check `Array.isArray(element)` to decide whether to recurse or push to result.
